newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NSW Australia barley shipments to Saudi begin.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NSW Australia barley shipments to Saudi begin.

text.p: Barley shipments for Saudi Arabia would start loading from ports in the Australian state of New South Wales (NSW) next week, the NSW Grains Board said on Friday.
They are the earliest shipments of NSW new season grain, it said in a statement.
About 90,000 tonnes of feed barley for Saudi Arabia would be loaded on ships at Newcastle and Port Kembla, Grains Board chairman Graham Lawrence said.
The shipments equated to about A$15 million for NSW grain growers, he said.

"With harvest in full swing and silo deliveries and rail facilities in top gear, its a real boon to have our shipping programme commencing this early and start the stock clearance programme," he said.
The NSW Grains Board was in a strong marketing position with the large harvest coming in, he said.
"We have confirmed sales to a number of destinations in the Asian region and look forward to maintaining a regular shipping programme from now on," he said.

With about 95 percent of barley deliveries to the Grains Board pools so far, recent volatility in the grains market had caused growers to weigh up the advantages of "across the year prices" generated by the pools against cash prices available on the day, he said.
The NSW Grains Board set strong pre-harvest prices for malt and feed barley that established a standard with interstate barley traders, he said.
The board's marketing and hedging positions enabled it to hold its barley prices, he said.

Barley marketing also was being greatly assisted by a cool finish to the growing season which allowed a long process of protein conversion. The general quality of malt and feed barley was the best in more than five years, he said.
With the canola harvest also starting, early tests indicated an average quality above last year, he added.
